task.title: Smart Notification Batching to Reduce Alert Fatigue
task.description:
## Idea: Smart Notification Batching to Reduce Alert Fatigue
- **User value**: Enterprise teams using TRACE get flooded when a deploy causes 50+ errors simultaneously. Each triggers an independent notification per rule, burying the signal in noise. Batching related alerts into a single digest-style notification keeps on-call engineers focused.
- **Rough scope**: Medium — new batching logic in notification worker + config UI
- **Suggested pipeline**: development
- **Sketch**: Add a configurable batching window (e.g. 60s default) to notification rules. When multiple triage results match the same rule within the window, collapse them into a single notification with a count and top-3 error summary. Store batch state in Redis with TTL. Add a "Batching" toggle + window-size input to the notification rule editor in SettingsModal. Slack/email templates get a "grouped" variant showing error count, severity breakdown, and a link to filtered incident queue.
- **Out of scope (for the v1 of this idea)**: Cross-rule batching, ML-based grouping, custom batch templates per channel.

task.title: Semantic Core
task.description:
# TRACE. — Semantic Core Feature Analysis
> Type: Feature Spec  
> Status: v2 — post verification review  
> Updated: 2026-04-14

---

## 1. Feature Definition

**Semantic Core** is an org-knowledge indexing layer that makes TRACE.'s existing SOLVE feature context-aware. Instead of generic AI root-cause suggestions, SOLVE gains access to the org's own runbooks, wikis, and project documentation — so every suggestion is grounded in *what this team actually knows and does*.

**One-line:** Give SOLVE your org's brain. Get answers that know your stack.

### What it is NOT
- Not a standalone knowledge base tool
- Not a documentation search engine the user opens manually
- It's invisible infrastructure that makes every SOLVE response smarter

---

## 2. Problem It Solves

Current SOLVE behavior: LLM sees the error fingerprint, stack trace, and frequency data → produces general suggestions.

The gap: It doesn't know that *this org* has a runbook for `redis.connection.refused`, or that the last three times `payments.timeout` fired, the fix was in the gateway config, or that ServiceNow ticket INC0042187 is the same class of incident that took down prod six weeks ago.

**Semantic Core closes that gap.** The org's documented knowledge becomes part of every triage decision.

---

## 3. System Architecture

### 3.1 Pipeline Overview

```
                  INGESTION PIPELINE
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                              │
│  Confluence  ──┐                             │
│  Internal wiki ┤──► Document Processor       │
│  Runbooks ─────┤    (chunk + metadata tag)   │
│  Uploaded PDFs ┤         │                  │
│  Images/diagrams┘         ▼                  │
│                    Embedding Model           │
│                    (text + multimodal)       │
│                         │                   │
│                         ▼                   │
│                   Vector Store               │
│               (pgvector in PostgreSQL)       │
│                    + Metadata Index          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

                  RETRIEVAL PIPELINE (at triage time)
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                              │
│  Error group (fingerprint + stack + freq)    │
│       │                                      │
│       ▼                                      │
│  Query Constructor ──► Semantic Search       │
│       +              (similarity filter:     │
│  ServiceNow ticket    score ≥ 0.75)          │
│       │                   │                  │
│       │             Top-K chunks             │
│       │             (max 5, deduped)          │
│       └───────────────────┤                 │
│                           ▼                  │
│                  Context Injector            │
│              (sanitized, parameterized)      │
│                           │                  │
│                           ▼                  │
│                  LLM (SOLVE response)         │
│             grounded in org-specific docs    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Similarity threshold:** Only chunks with cosine similarity ≥ 0.75 are injected into the SOLVE prompt. Chunks below this threshold are dropped silently and logged for retrieval quality analysis.

### 3.2 ServiceNow Flow (Incident-Triggered Path)

```
  Engineer creates SNOW ticket
         │
         ▼
  TRACE. receives webhook (HMAC-SHA256 verified)
         │
         ▼
  Extract: affected services, error description,
           priority, CI (configuration item)
         │
         ▼
  Semantic search against org's indexed docs
  (runbooks for that service, past postmortems)
  using same similarity threshold (≥ 0.75)
         │
         ▼
  LLM generates enriched triage block:
  - Root cause hypotheses (ranked)
  - Relevant runbook references (cited)
  - Similar past incidents
  - Recommended first actions
         │
         ▼
  Push result back as SNOW work note
```

---

## 4. Document Sources & Ingestion

### 4.1 Supported Source Types

| Source | Format | Ingestion Method |
|--------|--------|-----------------|
| Confluence | Pages, spaces | REST API (OAuth 2.0 — read-only scopes) |
| Internal wikis | Markdown, HTML | File upload or API |
| Runbooks / SOPs | Markdown, PDF, DOCX | File upload |
| Project docs | PDF, DOCX, MD | File upload |
| Architecture images | PNG, SVG, JPG | Vision model → caption → embed |

### 4.2 File Size Limits
- **Upload limit per document:** 100 MB
- **Max chunks per org (MVP):** 50,000 chunks (~500 average-size documents)
- **Max chunks per org (Phase 3):** 1,000,000 chunks
- Documents exceeding chunk limit are rejected with a clear error; org admin is notified

### 4.3 Document Processing Steps

1. **Fetch** — pull source content (Confluence API call, file read, etc.)
2. **Validate** — reject files >100 MB; reject unsupported formats
3. **Extract** — strip formatting, extract text; for images, run vision embedding or OCR+caption (see §4.5)
4. **Chunk** — split into segments (target: 512–800 tokens per chunk, respect section boundaries)
   - Overlap: 100 tokens between adjacent chunks to preserve context
   - Overlap chunks are stored as separate rows; deduplication at query time by filtering adjacent chunks from same document sorted by `(documentId, chunkIndex)`
   - Code blocks are kept as atomic chunks — never split mid-code
5. **Tag** — attach metadata: `source_type`, `service_name`, `team`, `last_updated`, `doc_type`
6. **Classify** — LLM micro-call (see Prompt 1) to determine `doc_type` and extract service/team names; 3 retries with exponential backoff before marking as `doc_type: "general"`
7. **Embed** — generate vector embedding per chunk via `text-embedding-3-small` (1536-dim)
8. **Store** — upsert to `DocumentChunk` table with pgvector embedding

### 4.4 Confluence OAuth Scopes (read-only, no write access)
```
read:confluence-content.summary
read:confluence-content.all
read:space
```

### 4.5 Multimodal Handling

For image/diagram content (architecture diagrams, flow charts, screenshots):
- **Pass to:** `gpt-4o` with vision (max 5 MB per image; larger images rejected)
- **Generate:** Descriptive technical caption (max 500 tokens)
- **Embed:** Caption as text via standard embedding pipeline
- **Store:** `image_url` in chunk `metadata` for retrieval citation
- **Fallback:** If vision call fails, store `[Image: {filename} | {doc_title}]` as placeholder

---

## 5. Database Schema Additions

These additions extend the existing Prisma/PostgreSQL schema in `traceback`.

**Prerequisite migration:**
```sql
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
```

```prisma
model OrgDocument {
  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  orgId        String
  sourceType   SourceType
  sourceUrl    String?
  title        String
  docType      DocType
  rawContent   String?
  lastSyncedAt DateTime
  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime   @updatedAt

  chunks       DocumentChunk[]

  @@index([orgId])
  @@index([orgId, sourceType])
}

model DocumentChunk {
  id         String      @id @default(cuid())
  orgId      String      // denormalized for direct org-scoped queries — no join required
  documentId String
  document   OrgDocument @relation(fields: [documentId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  content    String
  embedding  Unsupported("vector(1536)")
  chunkIndex Int
  metadata   Json        // { service_name?, team?, tags[], section_title?, image_url? }
  createdAt  DateTime    @default(now())

  @@index([orgId])
  @@index([documentId, chunkIndex])  // efficient pagination within a document
  // pgvector index — add via raw migration (not Prisma schema):
  // CREATE INDEX ON "DocumentChunk" USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (lists = 100);
}

model SemanticCoreConfig {
  id              String    @id @default(cuid())
  orgId           String    @unique
  confluenceUrl   String?
  // tokens stored AES-256-GCM encrypted — never plaintext. See §9 Encryption.
  confluenceToken String?
  snowEnabled     Boolean   @default(false)
  snowInstance    String?
  snowToken       String?
  snowWebhookSecret String? // HMAC-SHA256 verification secret for webhook endpoint
  syncIntervalHrs Int       @default(24)
  lastSyncAt      DateTime?
  chunkCount      Int       @default(0)
  maxChunks       Int       @default(50000)
  createdAt       DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime  @updatedAt
}

enum SourceType {
  confluence
  wiki
  runbook
  pdf
  image
}

enum DocType {
  runbook
  postmortem
  architecture
  sop
  general
}
```

**pgvector index note:** The IVFFlat index cannot be defined in Prisma schema syntax. Add via raw SQL migration:
```sql
CREATE INDEX ON "DocumentChunk"
  USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
  WITH (lists = 100);
-- lists = sqrt(total_rows) is a good default. Increase at 1M+ rows.
```

---

## 6. Encryption — Credential Fields

All `*Token` and `*Secret` fields in `SemanticCoreConfig` are encrypted at the application layer before writing to the database. Never stored in plaintext.

**Implementation:**
- Library: Node.js built-in `crypto` module — `createCipheriv` / `createDecipheriv` with `aes-256-gcm`
- Key: 32-byte key from environment variable `SEMANTIC_CORE_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
- IV: 12-byte random IV generated per encryption, stored prepended to the ciphertext
- Auth tag: 16-byte GCM auth tag stored appended to ciphertext
- Format in DB: `base64(iv + ciphertext + tag)` — single string column

```typescript
// src/lib/encryption.ts
import { randomBytes, createCipheriv, createDecipheriv } from "crypto";

const ALGO = "aes-256-gcm";
const KEY = Buffer.from(process.env.SEMANTIC_CORE_ENCRYPTION_KEY!, "base64");

export function encrypt(plaintext: string): string {
  const iv = randomBytes(12);
  const cipher = createCipheriv(ALGO, KEY, iv);
  const encrypted = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(plaintext, "utf8"), cipher.final()]);
  const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();
  return Buffer.concat([iv, encrypted, tag]).toString("base64");
}

export function decrypt(ciphertext: string): string {
  const buf = Buffer.from(ciphertext, "base64");
  const iv = buf.subarray(0, 12);
  const tag = buf.subarray(buf.length - 16);
  const encrypted = buf.subarray(12, buf.length - 16);
  const decipher = createDecipheriv(ALGO, KEY, iv);
  decipher.setAuthTag(tag);
  return Buffer.concat([decipher.update(encrypted), decipher.final()]).toString("utf8");
}
```

Apply in Prisma middleware or service layer — never allow raw token values to be returned from API responses.

---

## 7. API Changes

### 7.1 New Routes (in `traceback` Lens app)

| Method | Route | Auth | Rate Limit | Description |
|--------|-------|------|-----------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/semantic-core/sync` | Session required | 1/min per org | Trigger full re-index of org docs |
| POST | `/api/semantic-core/documents` | Session required | 10/min per org | Upload a document manually |
| GET  | `/api/semantic-core/documents` | Session required | 60/min | List indexed documents with status |
| DELETE | `/api/semantic-core/documents/[id]` | Session required | 10/min | Remove document from index |
| GET  | `/api/semantic-core/config` | Session required | 60/min | Get org's Semantic Core config |
| PATCH | `/api/semantic-core/config` | Session required | 10/min | Update config (tokens encrypted on write) |
| POST | `/api/semantic-core/search` | **Internal only** — middleware blocks external calls | 100/min per org | Retrieve top-K chunks (used by SOLVE, not public) |
| POST | `/api/webhooks/servicenow` | HMAC-SHA256 signature verified | 100/min per org | Receive SNOW incident webhook |

**`/api/semantic-core/search` — Internal Guard:**
```typescript
// Middleware: src/middleware.ts
// Block external access to search endpoint
if (req.nextUrl.pathname === "/api/semantic-core/search") {
  const internalToken = req.headers.get("x-internal-token");
  if (internalToken !== process.env.INTERNAL_API_SECRET) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "forbidden" }, { status: 403 });
  }
}
```

### 7.2 ServiceNow Webhook Security

```typescript
// src/app/api/webhooks/servicenow/route.ts
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "crypto";

async function verifySnowSignature(
  payload: string,
  signature: string,
  secret: string
): Promise<boolean> {
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(payload)
    .digest("hex");
  const sigBuf = Buffer.from(signature, "hex");
  const expBuf = Buffer.from(expected, "hex");
  if (sigBuf.length !== expBuf.length) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(sigBuf, expBuf); // constant-time comparison
}

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const payload = await req.text();
  const signature = req.headers.get("x-snow-signature") ?? "";
  const config = await getOrgSnowConfig(req); // org lookup by webhook URL or token
  const valid = await verifySnowSignature(payload, signature, decrypt(config.snowWebhookSecret!));
  if (!valid) return Response.json({ error: "invalid signature" }, { status: 401 });
  // ... proceed
}
```

**Token rotation:** Org admins can rotate `snowWebhookSecret` in TRACE. settings. Old secret is invalidated immediately.

### 7.3 Modified Routes

- **`POST /api/solve/[errorGroupId]`** — now accepts optional `useSemanticCore: boolean` flag. If `true` and Semantic Core is configured for the org, calls retrieval pipeline before LLM call.

---

## 8. Cost Estimates (MVP)

**Embedding costs (OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` @ $0.02/1M tokens):**

| Scale | Documents | Avg chunks/doc | Total chunks | Tokens (800 avg) | One-time cost |
|-------|-----------|----------------|--------------|-------------------|---------------|
| Small org pilot | 200 docs | 80 | 16,000 | 12.8M | **$0.26** |
| Mid org | 1,000 docs | 100 | 100,000 | 80M | **$1.60** |
| Large org | 10,000 docs | 100 | 1,000,000 | 800M | **$16.00** |

**Re-indexing (24h schedule):** Cost scales with changed documents only (delta sync). Estimated $2–15/month per mid-large org.

**Vision model (gpt-4o for image captions):** ~$0.01/image for typical architecture diagrams. Only triggered for image/diagram uploads.

**LLM augmentation (SOLVE):** Adds ~2K tokens of retrieved context per SOLVE call. At $5/1M tokens (gpt-4o), ~$0.01 per augmented SOLVE call. Negligible.

---

## 9. Feature Scope — MVP vs Full

### MVP (Phase 1)
- Manual document upload (PDF, MD, DOCX, PNG)
- Text chunking, classification, embedding
- pgvector for storage (no new infra)
- SOLVE augmentation when docs are present (similarity ≥ 0.75)
- Basic Semantic Core settings UI in Lens
- Internal `/api/semantic-core/search` endpoint

### Phase 2
- Confluence API sync (OAuth 2.0, read-only)
- Auto re-indexing on configurable schedule
- ServiceNow webhook integration
- Retrieval citations shown in SOLVE output UI
- PROMPT 7 relevance evaluator (active filtering)
- Deduplication evaluator for overlapping chunks

### Phase 3
- Multi-source sync management (multiple Confluence spaces, multiple wikis)
- Custom tagging UI (service/team labels on docs)
- Retrieval quality feedback loop (thumbs on context relevance)
- Index size dashboard (chunk count, last sync, coverage gaps)
- Chunk limit increase to 1M per org
- Migration to Qdrant/Pinecone if org volume exceeds pgvector sweet spot (~5M chunks)

---

## 10. Key Technical Decisions

### Vector DB: pgvector
- Zero new infrastructure — runs on existing PostgreSQL
- IVFFlat index handles 1M+ vectors with acceptable latency (~20ms p99)
- Decision: abstract behind a `VectorStore` interface for clean swap to Qdrant/Pinecone at scale

### Embedding Model: `text-embedding-3-small`
- 1536-dim, strong semantic accuracy
- ~$0.02/1M tokens — negligible for typical enterprise doc volume
- Multimodal: `gpt-4o` vision → caption text → embed caption via same model

### Chunking
- Target: 512–800 tokens, 100-token overlap
- Split priority: section heading → paragraph → sentence → hard cut at 800
- Atomic: code blocks never split mid-block
- Overlap deduplication: at query time, sort by `(documentId, chunkIndex)`, filter adjacent duplicates before injecting

### Security
- All credential fields encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM, key from env)
- Per-org query isolation: every vector search scoped by `orgId` WHERE clause (denormalized on chunk for zero-join isolation)
- `/api/semantic-core/search` blocked by internal token middleware
- Webhook signature verified via HMAC-SHA256 with constant-time comparison

---

## 11. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Stale docs poison SOLVE answers | Show `lastSyncedAt` in UI; warn when docs >30 days old; badge on SOLVE output |
| Low retrieval quality misleads SOLVE | Similarity threshold ≥ 0.75; log all dropped chunks for quality analysis |
| Large orgs exceed chunk limits | MVP cap at 50K chunks; notify org admin when 80% full; Phase 3 raises to 1M |
| Multimodal images too large | Reject >5 MB images at upload; fallback caption for failed vision calls |
| ServiceNow webhook spoofing | HMAC-SHA256 signature verification; constant-time comparison (no timing attacks) |
| Prompt injection via chunk content | Content sanitized before injection; parameterized template (no raw string replace) |
| Overlap chunks cause SOLVE duplication | Adjacent chunk deduplication at query time before context injection |
| Encryption key compromise | Key rotated via env var change + re-encryption job; no plaintext in logs |
| False "no docs found" on retrieval | Fallback: if 0 chunks ≥ 0.75, lower threshold to 0.65 and retry once; if still 0, note gap in SOLVE output |
| Developer misconfigures Confluence OAuth | Pre-defined read-only scope set in TRACE. OAuth registration; no write scopes possible |
